text:
customer-jane: hey, our prod traffic started hitting eu-west-1 from us-east-1 around 08:15 UTC, causing ~300ms extra tail latency and a spike in 5xxs. our api key is pinned to us-east-1. can you check?

alan_support: thanks for the report — we're looking. can you confirm the API key + project id? any recent config changes on your side?

customer-jane: same key, no infra changes. i see a few 502s and some 401s in the same window. billing shows requests billed to eu-west-1 for that minute.

alan_support: @kevin_eng @liz_sre tagging you — region routing seems to have fallback to eu-west even though priority is us-east. suspect failover policy mis-eval.

kevin_eng: past few deploys touched the policy parser. grabbing logs now. do we have the failover config from customer?

customer-jane: pasted their policy below (redacted):
```json
{"failover": [{"region":"us-east-1","priority":1,"weight":100,"sticky":true},{"region":"eu-west-1","priority":2,"weight":0,"sticky":false}],"sticky_ttl_secs":3600}
```

liz_sre: quick note — weight 0 on eu-west should just make it not get traffic except as a last resort. not sure why it got hits. pulling routing decision trace.

deploy-bot: routing-eval job #4021 finished for key project-acme-42 (trace-id: t-9c3). eval path: policy-parse -> sort-by-priority -> pick-by-weight -> sticky-check.

kevin_eng: i see the bug in the parser: UI sends priority as strings and we do lexicographic sort instead of numeric. example: ["1","10","2"] would sort -> ["1","10","2"] (wrong order). in this customer's case some priorities were stored as "01" and "1" depending on import path which triggered an off-by-one priority inversion.

alan_support: that would make eu-west appear higher priority?

kevin_eng: yes, because "2" < "10" in lexicographic vs numeric, and leading zeroes change order. combined with our sticky cookie matching region id (we store last-region string in cookie), requests previously served from eu-west got sticky reapplied and never rebalanced.

liz_sre: that also explains the 401s — token validation happens per-region and eu-west didn't have the customer's rotated key yet, so we saw transient auth failures. and billing shows eu-west because meter attaches to execution region.

customer-jane: ugh — so we're billed for eu-west because of the fallback misorder? what about rate limits and quotas?

billing-bot: billing note: meter entries are generated by region execution logs. if a request executes in eu-west it'll be billed there regardless of original region setting. we'll work with support for any adjustments if systemic.

kevin_eng: repro steps for us to validate: 1) import failover policy JSON with mixed numeric/string priorities 2) trigger a small burst forcing routing decisions 3) observe lexicographic sort result and sticky-cookie persistence 4) see auth 401s on target fallback region if keys not synced.

kevin_eng: quick patch idea: coerce priority to integer at parse time, normalize leading zeros, and publish a migration job that validates existing policies. also update tests to include string priorities.

liz_sre: mitigation for customer: 1) temporarily set sticky:false and weight:100 on us-east to force rebalancing 2) rotate keys to be identical across regions (if possible) to avoid auth failures during fallback 3) we'll roll a hotfix to the parser and push a config migration check.

alan_support: i've instructed the customer to set sticky:false and bumped us-east weight. they're applying now.

customer-jane: applied sticky:false and reweighted, traffic is shifting back to us-east. 5xxs dropping. thanks.

kevin_eng: creating PR with coercion + unit tests. tagging @deploy-bot for canary.

deploy-bot: canary deployed to staging-policy-parser-v2 (canary id c-77). running regression suite.

liz_sre: after canary passes, we'll run migration that scans all policies for non-integer priorities and normalize them. i'll coordinate a throttled rollout and runbook.

alan_support: customer is asking about credit for the burst billing. @billing-bot any suggestions?

billing-bot: support can submit a billing review ticket referencing trace-id t-9c3 and window 2025-11-17T08:15:00Z. include config snapshot. billing will triage.

kevin_eng: follow-up actions: - PR #487 (parser integer coercion) - migration job #m-112 queued - add unit tests for mixed-type priorities - sticky cookie change: store affinity token instead of raw region id - update docs warning about importing policies with padded numbers

liz_sre: assigning postmortem to kevin + alan. ETA for hotfix in prod: ~2h after canary clears. i'll stay on standby for rollout.

customer-jane: appreciate the fast turnaround. please keep me posted in this thread. :thumbsup:

alan_support: will do — closing interim loop once hotfix in prod and billing review opened.

kevin_eng: note for internal: potential related issue where UI exported CSV padded numbers. add sanitization in UI exporter.

liz_sre: logging action: add metric for "routing.policy.parse_errors" and an alert if policies parsed with non-numeric priorities > 0.

customer-jane: seeing steady 20ms p95 now, thanks team.

alan_support: great — thanks everyone.
